hazard_consequence_node.label: HazardConsequence
hazard_consequence_node.name: VCE
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: The report states that Tank 409 overflowed, gasoline 'formed a vapor cloud,' and at 12:23 a.m. 'the vapor cloud exploded, creating a pressure wave that damaged hundreds of homes and businesses up to 1.25 miles from the site.' The root cause section also identifies the physical cause as gasoline overflow resulting in 'a vapor cloud formation' that 'ignited in the WWT area.'
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: The central accident mechanism analyzed is a large gasoline vapor cloud formed by tank overfill, migrated across the site, and then exploded. The subsequent fires and secondary tank explosions are described as escalation effects, but the report's main causal analysis focuses on the vapor cloud explosion.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: gasoline
entity_nodes.explanation: Gasoline was the released flammable material that formed the vapor cloud and drove the explosion scenario.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: Tank 409
entity_nodes.explanation: Tank 409 was the storage tank that overfilled and released gasoline.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: wastewater treatment (WWT) area
entity_nodes.evidence: recorded the ignition of the vapor cloud in the WWT area
entity_nodes.explanation: The vapor cloud ignited in the wastewater treatment area after migrating from the tank farm.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: Vapor
condition_nodes.explanation: The hazardous state driving the VCE was a gasoline vapor cloud.

condition_nodes.label: Temperature
condition_nodes.name: Atmospheric temperature
condition_nodes.evidence: With a light breeze of about 5 mph on a 79ºF night
condition_nodes.explanation: The release and dispersion occurred under ambient outdoor nighttime temperature conditions.

condition_nodes.label: Volatility
condition_nodes.name: High volatility
condition_nodes.evidence: escaped gasoline formed a low-lying vapor cloud
condition_nodes.explanation: The gasoline readily vaporized and formed a large flammable vapor cloud.

condition_nodes.label: Combustibility
condition_nodes.name: Combustible
condition_nodes.evidence: The vapor cloud ignited in the WWT area
condition_nodes.explanation: The released gasoline vapor was flammable and ignited, producing the explosion and fires.

condition_nodes.label: ReleaseType
condition_nodes.name: Continuous release
condition_nodes.evidence: Tank 409 overflowed for an estimated 26 minutes before the vapor cloud ignited
condition_nodes.explanation: The gasoline release occurred over several minutes as an ongoing tank overflow rather than as an instantaneous release.

condition_nodes.label: Confinement
condition_nodes.name: Low confinement
condition_nodes.evidence: formed a low-lying vapor cloud that encompassed an area equivalent to 107 acres
condition_nodes.explanation: The vapor cloud spread across large outdoor tank farm and wastewater treatment areas, indicating low confinement.

condition_nodes.label: Dispersion
condition_nodes.name: Dispersed
condition_nodes.evidence: formed a low-lying vapor cloud that encompassed an area equivalent to 107 acres
condition_nodes.explanation: The released gasoline dispersed widely as a vapor cloud before ignition.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Tank 409 overfill during gasoline transfer
event_nodes.explanation: The accident sequence began when Tank 409 overfilled during ship-to-shore gasoline transfer.

event_nodes.label: MechanicalFailure
event_nodes.name: Tank 409 side gauge malfunction
event_nodes.evidence: Malfunctioning tank side gauge during filling operations that led to inaccurate tank levels being recorded
event_nodes.explanation: The malfunctioning side gauge was the key equipment failure identified as contributing to the overfill and subsequent loss of containment.
